ceilingHistory: Lane J, 2026-09-02: skyline-terminal 3 -> 0 and gun-range 2 -> 0. Two consequences worth stating plainly. gun-range's 0 is only meaningful ALONGSIDE the `gun-range-wallbang-walkthrough-panels` annotation, because the ceiling now judges unannotated rows only - drop the annotation and the arena measures 2 against a ceiling of 0. skyline-terminal's 0 was measured against a nacelle collider footprint this same lane proved transposed against its visual (F1, not landed), so it certifies the pre-F1 footprint and will very likely move when F1 lands; the lane that lands it fixes geometry, it does not raise this back. Both moved DOWN, to the value measured after the fixes in this pass; no ceiling in this file has ever been raised to make a spot green and none was raised here. map3 -1 (unmeasured sentinel) -> 0 is its FIRST real measurement, not a forgiveness: 3,516 legal hug spots, 24,612 traces, zero violations. atomic-acres stays 15 (measured 15, its access-ramp fringe class is Lane A/U territory) and high-seas stays 2 though it measured 0 today, because one clean run on somebody else's arena is not this lane's mandate to ratchet.
unverifiedCeilingNote: Lane J repair, 2026-09-02. Stage 3 reports a row it could not measure (the stance machine refused the stance, or the teleported body had not settled when the seat was read) as UNVERIFIED rather than scoring the missing measurement as distance 0 - reading a hole as a clip is the mistake that produced 51 of this pass's red rows. But UNVERIFIED with no cap is worse: a regression that pushes every row into that bucket produces a fully green stage 3 that measured nothing, which is the exact 'green gate that never looked' class this repo keeps hitting. So the count is ratcheted per arena exactly like the violation ceiling: an arena with no allowance may have none, more than the allowance FAILS, and the numbers here are what the instrument measured, not a budget. Seven arenas are at 0. atomic-acres is at 4: its four exterior-access-ramp rows (stand/crouch, sweep d=0.053-0.099) come back `stance-blocked:prone` - the body LANDS fine (settled in 10-20 frames) and the real stance machine then refuses to leave prone under the ramp overhang, i.e. the sweep's legality model says a player can stand there and the shipped character controller says they cannot. That is the same class-(b) instrument gap as the gun-range door, on an arena Lane J does not own; it is recorded as a number rather than a warning so the atomic-acres lane inherits a ratchet, not a shrug. May hold or shrink, never grow. HF-423 (PASS 87): farcrysis enters this table at 0. Lane R committed no unverified allowance, and an allowance is a MEASUREMENT, not a budget - so it enters at the tightest legal value rather than at a number back-derived from its 241 never-teleported stage-3 rows. Stage 3 against farcrysis is therefore RED until those rows are either fixed or measured and signed for; that is the honest state, not a passing one.

farcrysis.note: MEASURED from docs/evidence/pass87/lane-r/eye-clearance-stage2-violations.json: 441 rows total, 373 of them naming farcrysis-terrain-proxy-* (the ground), 68 naming the arena's own colliders - farcrysis-art-tower-platform-collider 23, farcrysis-core-catwalk 20, farcrysis-vantage-02-base-* 15, farcrysis-art-cave-arch-top-collider 3, farcrysis-enhanced-palm-trunk-collider-* 5, farcrysis-ruined-wall-sw-a 1, farcrysis-crate-08 1. The 441 raw ceiling is the honest measurement and stays, but ~85% of it is the stage-1 flat-ground eye seat, so on its own it would let the arena's real row count grow more than fivefold without firing. This sub-ceiling is a TIGHTENING added the same day the raw one was recorded, not a re-baseline: it is set AT the measured arena-side value with no slack. When stage 1 learns to seat eye heights on an arena's own heightfield, the raw count collapses toward this one and this becomes the binding gate; do not raise it to absorb that change.

arenaSideCeilingsNote: Per-arena sub-ceiling on the violations that do NOT name a known instrument-artefact surface class. Enforced alongside `ceilings` by scripts/qa/sweep-eye-clearance-live.mjs --check (see arenaSideCeiling / countArenaSideViolations in scripts/qa/eye-clearance-roster.mjs). An arena with no entry here is ratcheted on its raw count only; an entry with an empty exclusion list or a non-integer ceiling THROWS rather than passing vacuously. Excluding a class from this count never excuses it - the rows stay in the raw ceiling.

eyeModelDivergence.source: src/legacy-main.ts: `camera.position.y = Math.max(player.position.y + stanceTransitionSample.eyeOffsetMeters + 0.14, camera.position.y);` (the eyeOffset term is HF-412's drop-shot transition, 0 outside a prone transition) - the floor/terrain near-plane standoff, applied after bob/shake/trauma and BEFORE resolveEyeClearance. `player.position` is the eye (teleportPlayer calls characterPhysics.teleportEye), so the shipped camera sits a flat 0.14 m above the stance eye height every stage in this pipeline models.
eyeModelDivergence.measured: Reproduced on three arenas and three stances in one run, with the resolve idle or accounted for: gun-range crouch model 1.16 -> seat 1.300 (pushedM 0); atomic-acres prone model 0.61 -> seat 0.505 with pushedM 0.2449 (pre-push 0.7499); skyline-terminal prone model 0.61 -> seat 0.630 with pushedM 0.1201 (pre-push 0.7501). A constant +0.14 in every case, independent of stance and arena.
eyeModelDivergence.consequence: The sweep is OPTIMISTIC about overhead surfaces by 0.14 m and conservative about floor-level fringes by the same amount. It is why the skyline nacelle's 0.17 m analytic prone clearance still leaves the real camera 0.03 m under the belly before resolveEyeClearance pushes it back down to 0.63 - which the forcedProbes measure on every run. NOT changed here: re-modelling the eye moves every arena's numbers and needs its own pass with its own re-baseline. Pinned instead, so the constant cannot drift without this record being updated (scripts/qa/eye-clearance-sweep-contract.test.mjs).

closedRegressions.triage: 51 of the 55 were ONE probe artefact (class b) and 4 were the intentional wallbang fixtures (class c). Not one was a map defect. The test-bay secure door leaf is authored solid:false, shots:false because its authority is the door STATE: gunRangeTestBayDoorLeafBounds feeds both gunRangeTestBayDoorDynamicColliders (movement) and gunRangeTestBayDoorDynamicBallisticSurfaces (shots), and legacy-main splices the latter into activeBallisticSurfaces for gun-range. Stage 2 therefore traced against the closed leaf while stage 1's legality model could not see it, so the sweep emitted hug spots at x=51.10-51.12 - 0.03-0.05 m west of the leaf's 51.15 face, where a 0.36-0.38 m capsule sits a third of a metre INSIDE the closed door. Stage 3 corroborated it independently before the fix: teleporting the real player to those spots pushed it out of the leaf (seat x 51.00) and 50 of the 51 rows resolved. The FIX is to the probe, not to the map or the ceiling: sweep-eye-clearance-spots.ts now merges the same state-posed authority stage 2 can hit (dynamicAuthorityColliders), so gun-range emits 2,904 legal spots instead of 2,944 and those 40 illegal ones are gone.

All six were the same REAL geometry defect (class a), on both jetliner engine nacelles: the nacelle body spanned y 0.65..2.55 while the wing it hangs from is authored at 2.68..2.96, so the engines floated 0.13 m clear of the wing AND left a prone crawl space over a 0.61 m prone eye - analytic clearance 0.067 m, inside the 0.08 m camera near plane. Stage 3 was worse than the analytic number, not better: with nothing lateral to give, resolveEyeClearance pushed the camera UP into the nacelle to its 0.34 m cap (seat y 1.66, a metre above the player's real eye, looking through the engine's interior) and still measured 0.035 m. Fixed by seating the nacelle against the wing underside (centre y 1.6 -> 1.73, translation only, collider and instanced visual together): top lands exactly on 2.68, belly rises to 0.78, ANALYTIC prone clearance 0.17 m - past the 0.15 m probe radius. What the runtime then does is measured by the `forcedProbes` entries, not deduced: the first report of this lane said the resolve 'no longer engages there at all' and the lane's own capture receipts showed it engaging at all three sampled seats, two of them at the 0.34 m push cap. Those captures were themselves taken mid-fall (stage 3 now settles the body before reading a seat), but the honest state of the claim is: analytic VERIFIED, runtime measured by forced probe on every run.
